title: scl is eventually linear under stabilisation along a boundary curve
body:
## The conjecture

Let S be a surface with one boundary component gamma, and let alpha be an element
of the commutator subgroup. Then scl(alpha gamma^n) is eventually linear in n as n
tends to infinity.

## What supports it

The case where S is the modular orbifold is a theorem of Calegari and Louwsma,
recorded separately, and is generalised there to hyperbolic
(2,p,infinity)-orbifolds. The conjecture in the free group case originates as
Conjecture 3.16 of Calegari, *Faces of the scl norm ball*, supported by computer
experiment on the once-punctured torus.

## Why it bears on the winding obstruction

This is the reason for recording it here, and it is a hope rather than an
argument.

The obstruction to the cut-and-glue approach to rationality in closed surface
groups is that a boundary component of a candidate surface may wind around the
cutting curve an uncontrolled number of times, so that the search is not evidently
over a finite set. The winding number is precisely a stabilisation parameter of
the kind above.

Eventual linearity in that parameter would say that the unboundedness is tame:
beyond some finite point the behaviour is governed by a linear function, so one
would not have to search unboundedly, only far enough to reach the linear regime
and then compute the slope. That is the sense in which this could circumvent, or
at least tame, the non-finiteness.

What is missing to make this work is quantitative: eventual linearity alone does
not say where the linear regime starts, and a rationality argument would need that
threshold to be effective and uniform over the relevant chains or over a single
loop which has many large gamma^{n_i} subwords.
